# Degree of an Array.

@example 0 occurs three times, more than any other value; the shortest stretch holding all three 0s runs from index 1 to index 5.
[5,0,5,7,0,0,9]
=> 5

@example 2 and 6 both occur three times. The 6s fit in the stretch from index 1 to index 5; the 2s need all 7 elements.
[2,6,7,2,6,6,2]
=> 5

@example Every value occurs once, so the degree is 1, and a single element already reaches it.
[12,7,30]
=> 1

# A single element, the value 0.
[0]
=> 1

# All values different, degree 1: the answer is 1, not the whole length.
[8,2,6,4]
=> 1

# All equal.
[5,5,5,5]
=> 4

# The most common value at index 0 and at the last index. A table of first
# positions that uses 0 for "not seen yet" forgets the 6 at index 0.
[6,1,6]
=> 3

# 1 occurs twice side by side, but 4 occurs three times: only 4's stretch
# reaches the degree.
[9,4,6,4,1,1,4,8]
=> 6

# Four values tie at two copies each. The shortest stretch belongs to 4,
# which is neither the first value seen, nor the smallest, nor the largest,
# and is the third to reach two copies.
[6,2,6,9,2,4,4,9]
=> 2

# 0 is a value like any other.
[4,0,3,0]
=> 3

# The largest value allowed is the most common one: a table indexed by
# value needs 50000 slots.
[7,49999,3,49999]
=> 3

# 256 copies of 3, then an 8: a count kept in 8 bits wraps back to 0.
[3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,8]
=> 256

# 300 elements: 777 at index 0 and at index 299, all different values
# between them. Positions kept in 8 bits can't hold 299.
[777,1000,1001,1002,1003,1004,1005,1006,1007,1008,1009,1010,1011,1012,1013,1014,1015,1016,1017,1018,1019,1020,1021,1022,1023,1024,1025,1026,1027,1028,1029,1030,1031,1032,1033,1034,1035,1036,1037,1038,1039,1040,1041,1042,1043,1044,1045,1046,1047,1048,1049,1050,1051,1052,1053,1054,1055,1056,1057,1058,1059,1060,1061,1062,1063,1064,1065,1066,1067,1068,1069,1070,1071,1072,1073,1074,1075,1076,1077,1078,1079,1080,1081,1082,1083,1084,1085,1086,1087,1088,1089,1090,1091,1092,1093,1094,1095,1096,1097,1098,1099,1100,1101,1102,1103,1104,1105,1106,1107,1108,1109,1110,1111,1112,1113,1114,1115,1116,1117,1118,1119,1120,1121,1122,1123,1124,1125,1126,1127,1128,1129,1130,1131,1132,1133,1134,1135,1136,1137,1138,1139,1140,1141,1142,1143,1144,1145,1146,1147,1148,1149,1150,1151,1152,1153,1154,1155,1156,1157,1158,1159,1160,1161,1162,1163,1164,1165,1166,1167,1168,1169,1170,1171,1172,1173,1174,1175,1176,1177,1178,1179,1180,1181,1182,1183,1184,1185,1186,1187,1188,1189,1190,1191,1192,1193,1194,1195,1196,1197,1198,1199,1200,1201,1202,1203,1204,1205,1206,1207,1208,1209,1210,1211,1212,1213,1214,1215,1216,1217,1218,1219,1220,1221,1222,1223,1224,1225,1226,1227,1228,1229,1230,1231,1232,1233,1234,1235,1236,1237,1238,1239,1240,1241,1242,1243,1244,1245,1246,1247,1248,1249,1250,1251,1252,1253,1254,1255,1256,1257,1258,1259,1260,1261,1262,1263,1264,1265,1266,1267,1268,1269,1270,1271,1272,1273,1274,1275,1276,1277,1278,1279,1280,1281,1282,1283,1284,1285,1286,1287,1288,1289,1290,1291,1292,1293,1294,1295,1296,1297,777]

# 260 different values, then 5, 6, 5: the only value seen twice first
# occurs at index 260. A first position kept in 8 bits wraps to 4 and
# makes its stretch 259 long instead of 3.

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[49999,49999,0,49999,49999,49999,49999]
=> 7

@gen 2 small
[1,2,2,0,0]
=> 2

@gen 3 small
[0,0,0,0,0,0,49999,0]
=> 8

@gen 4 small
[0,0,49999,0]
=> 4

@gen 5 small
[1,2,4,4,4,3]
=> 3

@gen 6 small
[3,1]
=> 1

@gen 7 small
[0,0,49999,49999,0,49999]
=> 4
